xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5122: Terminal tab says 'conversation is not running' for Codex and OpenCode conversations on Herdr: the companion-terminal owner check is tmux-only

plan.title: Terminal tab says 'conversation is not running' for Codex and OpenCode conversations on Herdr: the companion-terminal owner check is tmux-only
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On a Herdr host every Codex or OpenCode conversation's Terminal tab (Native CLI) says 'The conversation is not running'. The companion-terminal host port only has a tmux implementation: createTmuxCompanionHost().ownerStamp runs `tmux has-session`, which never sees a Herdr pane, and index.ts wires that host unconditionally. Behind it, /ws/terminal on Herdr resolves terminals only by Herdr agent name or agentId token, so a Herdr companion would not attach either.
narratives.Proposal: Add a Herdr CompanionTerminalHost (herdr-host.ts): owner stamp from the Herdr probe (alive -> herdr:<paneId>, exited -> null, absent -> tmux fallback, indeterminate -> throw); companion = a tab in the `conversations` Herdr workspace stamped with dedicated `companion` and `companionGeneration` tokens (no agentId/role, so it is never an agent), running `<argv> ; exit` (not exec, so pane process liveness reads it as running). A delegating host (select-host.ts) picks Herdr or the unchanged tmux host per call from hostTerminalBackendName(). resolveHerdrTerminalId gains a companion branch that finds the pane by its token. Docs state the companion works on both backends. Full detail, before/after code and test names in .pan/drafts/pan-5122.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Changing the tmux companion host, its generation formula, or any tmux-host behavior
- Supporting a tmux host whose owner conversation runs on Herdr (rollback case)
- Reaping tmux companions left behind on a Herdr host
- Any change to packages/contracts, the companion-terminal routes, or the frontend ConversationTerminalView
- Stamping agentId, role, issue, harness or model tokens on a companion pane, or calling agent.rename for it
- Using launchAgentPane or TerminalBackend.startAgent for the companion
- Adding lines to src/lib/terminal-backends/herdr.ts or raising any file-size allowlist row
- Moving the ad-hoc terminal drawer onto Herdr
- New harness adapters

autoDecisions.summary: On a Herdr host the companion is a Herdr pane, not a tmux session.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's Fix names a Herdr host implementation, and tmux is not a prerequisite under Herdr (system-prerequisites.ts:361), so a tmux companion would fail on a Herdr host without tmux.

autoDecisions.summary: The companion pane carries only `companion` and `companionGeneration` tokens, no agentId/role/issue.
autoDecisions.rationale: Parity with tmux, where the companion- prefix is outside OVERDECK_SESSION_NAME and never an agent; an agentId token would put the companion in listHerdrAgents and the Agents Directory pane-only loop.

autoDecisions.summary: The Herdr pane runs `<quoted argv> ; exit` instead of `exec <argv>`.
autoDecisions.rationale: With exec the client takes the shell's pid, paneProcessLiveness reads it as exited, and the residue reaper would close a live companion.

autoDecisions.summary: Owner stamp: alive -> herdr:<paneId>; exited -> null; absent -> tmux stamp; indeterminate -> throw.
autoDecisions.rationale: Herdr pane ids are never reused; the absent fallback matches conversation-liveness.ts for pre-flip tmux owners; a null on a Herdr outage would reap a live companion and lie 'not running'.

autoDecisions.summary: Companions open in the `conversations` Herdr workspace.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is the workspace operator conversations already use (launch.ts CONVERSATIONS_WORKSPACE); the companion is an operator tool and must not be swept by an issue workspace close.

autoDecisions.summary: Host chosen per call from hostTerminalBackendName(); Herdr host loaded lazily.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps getCompanionTerminalLifecycle() synchronous, leaves the tmux path byte-for-byte unchanged, and avoids a static import edge that could trip lint:circular.

autoDecisions.summary: The issue's Herdr-host live acceptance (AC1/AC2) is a live verification item plus test-role browser UAT.
autoDecisions.rationale: The work agent cannot deploy its branch to the operator dashboard; a library-level live script plus the test role's isolated-browser UAT covers both halves.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD W1 exactly. Create src/lib/overdeck/companion-terminal/herdr-host.ts exporting COMPANION_NAME_TOKEN='companion', COMPANION_GENERATION_TOKEN='companionGeneration', herdrCompanionCommand(argv) (`${argv.map(shellQuoteArg).join(' ')} ; exit`, throws on empty argv), HerdrCompanionHostDeps, createHerdrCompanionHost(overrides) and findHerdrCompanionTerminalId(name, api?). ownerStamp per D4; readGeneration per D9; create per FR-3 (validateSessionName, ensureWorkspace -> 'conversations' Herdr workspace, openAgentTab with env {...spec.env, OVERDECK_COMPANION_GENERATION, TERM:'xterm-256color'} and label=name, then pane.report_metadata with source 'overdeck', tokens exactly {companion, companionGeneration}, title=name, then pane.send_input text=herdrCompanionCommand(argv) keys ['enter']; close the pane and rethrow on failure after the tab exists); kill per D8. All snapshot/process_info lookups use { timeoutMs: 2_000 }. Change `const CONVERSATIONS_WORKSPACE` to `export const` in launch.ts (no added lines). Do not add lines to herdr.ts. Write the eleven tests named in PRD W1 with an injected fake api (cast as unknown as HerdrApiClient), sizeTerminal and ensureWorkspace fakes.
narrative.Hazards: Tests must inject sizeTerminal (openAgentTab otherwise spawns the herdr binary). Never stamp agentId/role/issue on the companion.

narrative.Action: Implementation checkpoint from PRD W6. Find a running Codex conversation on this host. From the workspace, run a one-off `npx tsx` script (kept in the session scratchpad, not committed) that calls getCompanionTerminalLifecycle().open({ conversationName, ownerSession: 'conv-<name>', cwd, harness: 'codex' }), prints the result, checks `herdr pane list` for a pane titled companion-conv-<name>, calls resolveHerdrTerminalId('companion-conv-<name>') and prints the terminal id, then calls close(owner, generation) and confirms the pane is gone. Repeat for an OpenCode conversation if one runs. Never stop, resume, or message the owner conversation. Append a 'Live verification record — companion terminal on Herdr (PAN-5122)' section at the end of docs/TERMINAL-BACKENDS.md with the commands and outputs, in the style of the PAN-3974 record. Fallback: if no Codex/OpenCode conversation runs and none can be started on a scratch cwd under ~/Projects, the record states which checks could not run and why. Browser UAT is the test role's: isolated Playwright profile, on a Herdr host open a running Codex conversation -> Terminal -> Native CLI and confirm the Codex TUI renders with no 'not running' notice; same for OpenCode.
narrative.Hazards: The live script creates a real pane in the operator's Herdr session; close it at the end. Do not commit the script. If `npx tsx` fails on a circular ESM import (Node strict ESM), run the same script with `bun <script>.ts`; Bun tolerates the cycles.

items.title: Given a running Codex conversation on this Herdr host, when the live script calls open, then it prints status 'attached', `herdr pane list` shows a pane titled companion-conv-<name>, and resolveHerdrTerminalId returns a non-null terminal id; when it calls close with that generation, then the pane no longer appears (or the record states why the check could not run)
docs/TERMINAL-BACKENDS.md ends with a 'Live verification record — companion terminal on Herdr (PAN-5122)' section that shows each command and its observed output

Test-role browser UAT in an isolated Playwright profile: given a running Codex conversation on a Herdr host, when the operator opens Terminal -> Native CLI, then the native Codex TUI renders and no 'The conversation is not running' notice shows; the same holds for a running OpenCode conversation
